neighbours.label: suffix piece 'ons' or 'ated' after a split word stem (wag|ons, vac|ated, pige|ons)
fire: Every morning the old man fed the pigeons in the square.
The surgeon repaired two torn tendons in her knee.
The governor granted pardons to three prisoners.
My daughter drew a house with her new crayons.
By evening the storm had finally abated.
After the huge dinner everyone felt sated and sleepy.
The zookeepers confirmed the two pandas had mated.
He kept a flock of racing pigeons on the roof.
quiet: Every morning the old man fed the surgeons in the square.
The surgeon repaired two torn ligaments in her knee.
The governor handed coupons to three prisoners.
My daughter drew a house in the dungeons of the castle.
By evening the storm had finally dated.
After the huge dinner everyone felt full and sleepy.
The zookeepers confirmed the two pandas were situated nearby.
He kept a row of old cannons on the roof.

notes: Spelling unit. Card: 'ons' x6, 'ated' x2 (Wag|ons, vac|ated). Probe: wagons 0.69, vacated 0.81; ' dragons' as a whole token 0.07. Fire words chosen to split (pige|ons, tend|ons, pard|ons, cray|ons, ab|ated, s|ated, m|ated); near misses use words that are single tokens (surgeons, coupons, dungeons, gallons, situated, dated, gated, cannons).
